subs.text: This is KRIYA, live on Monad testnet.
A thousand-dollar test mandate, with hard limits: max risk forty, at most forty percent in any strategy, and a quarter in reserve.
Right now, forty percent sits in Strategy A, and thirty-five in Strategy C.
The external risk feed says Strategy C's risk just jumped, from fifteen to forty-five. That's above this mandate's limit.
So we run the real Chainlink CRE workflow, broadcasting to Monad.
CRE reads the feed with consensus, and writes the verified risk onchain, as a signed report.
It detects the mandate at risk.
Claude decides: exit C, keep A at its forty percent cap, and hold the rest in reserve.
The policy engine re-checks it inside the workflow, and CRE executes the rebalance onchain.
Back on the live dashboard: allocation number three, executed via Chainlink CRE.
Strategy C is now at zero, and portfolio risk dropped to nine, well inside the limit.
Both transactions are real, on Monad testnet, delivered through the Chainlink forwarder into KRIYA's executor.
And if the agent ever proposes something unsafe, like sixty percent in one strategy, the contract reverts it, onchain.
